text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- New local government structure emerges with delineation of Nigeria into 989 state constituencies, 860 federal seats and 109 senatorial districts for elections to restore democracy.
- Shell oil company restates in its newsletter that it will not resume oil production in volatile Ogoniland in the southeast for time being.
- Nigeria exports two billion naira worth of crude oil to Brazil in first half of 1996, Brazilian ambassador to Nigeria Geraldo Muzzi says at lecture on improving bilateral trade.
- Aviation minister Air Commodore Ita Udo-Imeh says federal government will help Nigeria Airways retrieve its DC-10 aircraft seized in U.S. for debt owed a U.S.-based maintenance company.
- Nigeria's chances of returning to Commonwealth brighten after visit of Commonwealth ministers this week on its suspension from the group for human rights abuses.
- Freed human rights activist Gani Fawehinmi recounts his ordeal in detention; colleague Femi Falana, also freed this week, says he may sue the government for his own detention.
- Maritime industry sources say government may allow private port terminals as part of port service reforms.

- International Monetary Fund sets three conditions -- merger of dual exchange rates, greater transparency in managing public finances and removal of oil subsidies -- for Nigeria to qualify for debt relief.
- Nigeria lost $268 million in cocoa exports to Japan over rigorous export procedures at ports and low quality of produce.
- Nigeria and Sudan plan to set up a gum arabic processing plant in Nigeria.
